scope.purpose: Define reusable governance constraints for production sheets, titleblocks, sheet identity, required sheet metadata, revision representation, composition, and pre-issue documentation quality without promoting unresolved source examples into canonical syntax.

requirements.statement: Production sheets shall use approved titleblock families from the governed content source.

A locally edited, duplicated, renamed, or otherwise non-governed titleblock variant shall not be relied upon for production output unless it has been accepted through the governed exception or change process.
Sheet numbers shall be unique within the governed project scope and shall use the applicable governed sheet-identity rule or approved project mapping.
Once a sheet identity has entered formal issue, it should remain stable through the project lifecycle; a post-issue identity change shall be documented through applicable change control.
A retired sheet number shall not be silently reused; reuse requires a documented reason and traceable change record.
Sheet names shall be human-readable, concise, descriptive of the primary content, and conform to the applicable governed naming vocabulary and syntax.
Client-specific or alternate sheet identifiers shall be stored in dedicated governed fields unless an approved project rule explicitly makes them part of the canonical sheet identity.

Every standard titleblock shall expose the required sheet, project, issue, revision, and responsibility data defined by the applicable governed parameter registry and project information requirements.
Required titleblock values shall be populated from governed project, parameter, role, issue, revision, and transmittal sources rather than locally invented substitutes.
New titleblock parameters or changes to governed titleblock parameters shall pass the applicable standards governance process before inclusion in standard titleblocks.
Governed revision information shall be represented through the Revit revision system and shall correspond to the applicable governed issue or transmittal record.
Ad-hoc titleblock text or manual graphical overrides shall not be used to substitute for governed revision information.
Each sheet should communicate a cohesive set of information and preserve sufficient visual context, spacing, and legibility for its declared use rather than maximizing content density.

Placed views shall use applicable approved view templates and governed view naming; per-view graphic overrides shall not be used unless the governing view standard explicitly permits them or an accepted exception records the reason.

Related plans, elevations, sections, details, legends, notes, north arrows, scale bars, and keynotes should be composed consistently across a sheet set using governed templates and annotation conventions.
Repeatable symbols, abbreviations, keynotes, legends, and general annotation shall use governed reusable content where available rather than uncontrolled duplicated graphics or text.
Floating or unanchored annotation that cannot be clearly associated with a view, legend, or governed sheet context shall not be used on production sheets.

Before formal issue, the applicable sheet set shall undergo pre-issue documentation QA covering titleblock identity, sheet identity and naming, required metadata, view-template compliance, annotation quality, revision state, and representative output legibility.
Changes to governed sheet-numbering rules, titleblock parameters, standard titleblock families, or reusable sheet-composition rules shall follow the BIM Standards governance and release process.

unresolved_source_items.source_evidence: The source proposes {DisciplineCode}{Series}-{Sequence} and example discipline/series codes but explicitly states that exact codes are to be finalized by the Standards Committee and contains TODOs.
unresolved_source_items.curator_treatment: Retain as source evidence only until a governed S4 vocabulary and syntax is approved.

unresolved_source_items.source_evidence: The source recommends {Level/Area} – {Content/Scope}, Title Case, and source examples, while other naming source material repeats the pattern without resolving the underlying TODO status.
unresolved_source_items.curator_treatment: Require governed human-readable naming without treating the proposed literal pattern as canonical.

unresolved_source_items.source_evidence: G-series, discipline+S, discipline+D, and discipline+3 examples are described as typical, proposed, or subject to local confirmation.
unresolved_source_items.curator_treatment: Do not promote example ranges or codes.

unresolved_source_items.source_evidence: The source calls one main plan view typical and explicitly leaves numeric limits and discipline exceptions as TODOs.
unresolved_source_items.curator_treatment: Promote the readability/cohesion principle only; do not invent a maximum view count.

unresolved_source_items.source_evidence: The source lists titleblock fields but repeatedly requires exact parameter names to resolve through the Shared Parameter Registry and contains unresolved links/TODOs.
unresolved_source_items.curator_treatment: Govern the obligation to expose required fields while leaving exact parameter identity to S8/project information requirements.

provenance.migration_note: Curated from mixed Confluence source material by separating normative sheet/titleblock constraints from L6 Revit execution. Explicit TODOs, proposed numbering codes, example ranges, unconfirmed organization-specific values, and draft export filename/folder examples were not promoted. During migration, Confluence remains source authority.
